newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: W.Australia defers gold royalty start - government.
newsitem.headline: W.Australia defers gold royalty start - government.

text.p: The Western Australian state government said on Monday it would defer the introduction of a planned gold royalty.
Premier Richard Court said the royalty would now be phased in from July 1, 1998, at a rate of 1.25 percent, representing a nine month delay from the original implementation date.
The state cabinet also agreed to make concessions relating to the introduction of the second stage of the royalty, which would be delayed 12 months to July 1, 2000.
"The full 2.5 percent rate will only come into effect if the average gold spot price is A$450 (an ounce) or more in the preceding quarter," Court said.
"This arrangement will be grandfathered to 2005," Court said.
He estimated the changes will save the industry up to A$18 million in the current financial year and a further A$36 million in the following two years.
The royalty will only apply to the spot price of gold, not the higher forward sales prices being realised by many mining companies, he said.
Safeguards for small producers had also been extended with an increase in the proposed production exemption threshold to 2,500 ounces from 1,000 ounces, Court said.
Temporary royalty relief also will be available to miners who experience cash-flow problems, he said.
Western Australia produces about 80 percent of Australia's annual gold production of nearly 300 tonnes.
